analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and supplied surrounding documentation against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. No independently supported security regression is established by these documentation-only units; runtime enforcement is not supplied.
changelog.d/autopilot-placements-and-busy-reasons.md:3-9 describes broader verified-model eligibility under saved consent, default-on background downloads with optional limits and a 50 GiB free-space floor, serving adoption beyond a control lease, bounded placement holds, richer heartbeats and transition watchdogs. Integration should verify consent/revocation gates and that adoption does not replace current App Attest serving authorization (A-016, T-052/T-053); catalog/build verification and invalidation (A-004, T-012/T-027); download accounting, concurrency and disk-reserve enforcement (T-016); and late completion fencing without releasing live native ownership (T-010, TB-007). These are unverified contracts, not observed missing controls.
docs/architecture/hardware-support.md head:351-355 excludes held slots from eviction and held weights from reclaim credit. This is consistent with conservative admission, while the changelog's 24-hour holds intentionally alter idle unloading (T-029). Integration should check every eviction/pre-accept path, including managed Nemotron Super, uses those exclusions and preserves process-ledger and reslice floors described in base:475-574. Watchdog cancellation must not be mistaken for actual native resource retirement.
No changed encryption, cache-scope, TTL, receipt, billing or privileged-helper control is visible. T-041's existing same-account timing risk and SSD disk guards remain relevant to newly eligible models and concurrent downloads, but no cache-policy weakening is shown. Existing memory-measurement limitations in surrounding documentation are not PR regressions. Implementation review must reconcile these new resource-control contracts with the threat model; this scope cannot validate the changelog's enforcement claims.
